chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, all together, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A group of sick people from the Banu Dabba arrived at the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'Stay with me, so when you are cured, I will send you in a raiding party.' They said, 'Take us out of the city.' So he sent them to the charity camels, drinking from their urine and eating from their milk. When they were cured and became strong, they killed three of those who were with the camels.

The news reached the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he sent Ali (peace be upon him) to them. They were in a valley, confused, unable to exit it, near the land of Yemen. So he captured them and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land.
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) chose the cutting, so he cut their hands and feet from opposite sides.

key_terms.إِبِلِ الصَّدَقَةِ: Charity camels, specifically those designated for zakat
key_terms.بَنِي ضَبَّةَ: Banu Dabba, a tribe from Yemen
key_terms.مِنْ خِلافٍ: From opposite sides (referring to hands and feet)
key_terms.يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ: Those who wage war against Allah

ai.seo_question: What was the punishment for the Banu Dabba after they rebelled and killed their caretakers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the historical incident of the Banu Dabba, whose apostasy and rebellion triggered the revelation of Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 33. It highlights the Prophet's discretionary choice (ikhtiyar) among the four punishments prescribed in the verse, specifically selecting the amputation of hands and feet from opposite sides, a ruling that Shia scholars often cite to discuss the flexibility of hadd penalties in specific contexts.
